columns.name: invoice_id
columns.description: Invoice number, kept as text (identifiers are text; Session D rule). A leading C marks a cancellation invoice; see is_cancellation.
columns.rationale: Committed required true matches profile null_rate 0.0; unchanged in this amendment.

columns.name: is_cancellation
columns.description: True when invoice_id carries the C cancellation prefix. Decision: cancellations are retained and flagged, not dropped, so conservation arithmetic against bronze stays auditable; exclusion is a consumer decision made at the mapping contract, not silently here.
columns.rationale: Committed required true matches profile null_rate 0.0; unchanged in this amendment.

columns.name: stock_code
columns.description: Product code as landed, kept as text; alphanumeric suffixes and non-product adjustment codes (for example POST, M) occur.
columns.rationale: Committed required true matches profile null_rate 0.0; unchanged in this amendment.

columns.name: product_description
columns.description: Product description, whitespace-trimmed. Nulls are retained rather than imputed.
columns.rationale: Profile shows null_rate 0.005098 (228 of 44721 rows), consistent with the committed optional flag; unchanged.

columns.name: quantity
columns.description: Units on the line, cast from DECIMAL(38,9) to INTEGER. Negative values occur both on cancellation-invoice lines and on zero-unit-price stock-adjustment lines; consumers must not infer cancellation from negative quantity alone.
columns.rationale: Profile null_rate 0.0 matches committed required true; unchanged.

columns.name: invoiced_at
columns.description: Invoice timestamp. Decision: strict cast from the VARCHAR landing ("YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS"); an unparseable value fails the build loudly rather than becoming a silent null. On within-invoice clock-drift duplicates the earliest scan tick wins (min).
columns.rationale: Profile null_rate 0.0 matches committed required true; unchanged.

columns.name: unit_price
columns.description: Unit price in sterling, cast from DECIMAL(38,9). Observed range 0.00 to 1998.49. Decision: zero-price lines (freebies and adjustments) are retained; negative prices are contract-invalid.
columns.rationale: Profile null_rate 0.0 and min 0.0 / max 1998.49 match the committed required flag and non-negative rule; unchanged.

columns.name: customer_id
columns.description: Customer identifier, cast DECIMAL(38,9) to INTEGER. Decision: the bronze null rate is retained as null (guest or unregistered checkouts), not dropped and not imputed.
columns.rationale: Profile null_rate 0.300664 confirms the committed optional flag; unchanged.

columns.name: country
columns.description: Customer country as landed (24 distinct values).
columns.rationale: Profile null_rate 0.0 and distinct_count 24 match the committed required flag; unchanged.

columns.name: captured_at
columns.description: Capture timestamp carried forward from the bronze landing (_airbyte_extracted_at), marking when the surviving line's earliest capture entered the pipeline. It is the incremental watermark the gold layer builds on and is now guaranteed present on every row, so consumers can rely on it without a null check.
columns.rationale: Fresh profile measures captured_at at null_rate 0.0 across all 44,721 rows (null_count 0), matching row_count exactly, confirming the incremental path has landed and the column is fully populated as the operator intent states.

quality_rules.rationale: Table holds 44,721 rows at profiling time; the never-empty expectation stands unchanged.
Grain (invoice_id, stock_code, quantity, unit_price) remains the enforced uniqueness key; unchanged by this amendment.
Profile min 0.0 confirms unit_price never goes negative; unchanged rule.

changes.rationale: Fresh profile measures captured_at null_rate 0.0 over 44,721 rows (null_count 0), fulfilling the v1.2.0-declared follow-up that tightening to required waits until the incremental path lands and the column is proven populated; operator intent confirms the incremental path has landed.

changes.before: Capture timestamp carried forward from the bronze landing (_airbyte_extracted_at): when the surviving line's earliest capture entered the pipeline. The incremental watermark the gold layer builds on (Record 008 part two, D-38). Enters optional under the F-28 rule; the declared follow-up tightens it to required once the incremental path lands and the column is proven populated. v1.2.0 adds this column and changes nothing else.
changes.after: Capture timestamp carried forward from the bronze landing (_airbyte_extracted_at), marking when the surviving line's earliest capture entered the pipeline. It is the incremental watermark the gold layer builds on and is now guaranteed present on every row, so consumers can rely on it without a null check.
changes.rationale: The optional-to-required tightening removes the prior caveat about eventual population; the fresh profile's null_rate 0.0 over 44,721 rows shows the column is now fully populated, so the description must describe meaning without the stale conditional language.

decisions.rationale: Profile null_rate 0.0 over 44,721 rows (matching row_count) confirms the v1.2.0-declared follow-up condition is met, so captured_at moves from optional to required.

purpose: The cleaned, typed, one-row-per-invoice-line view of the Online Retail II sample: the first contracted silver table and the sole silver input to the gold unified event star.
usage: Read silver.silver_invoice_lines for line-level retail sales analysis. Cancellation lines are RETAINED and flagged (is_cancellation); consumers aggregating revenue must filter or net them deliberately. Zero-price lines are retained.
limitations: Exact duplicate bronze rows are treated as capture artifacts and excluded, so identical legitimate re-scans are indistinguishable and also excluded; the residual grain is the distinct line. Rows identical in every business column except invoicedate are the same capture artifact seen across a register clock tick; they collapse to one line and the earliest timestamp is retained. customer_id remains null for guest or unregistered checkouts and those rows are retained with customer_id null.
